chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fazala, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, that Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

The one who is not married (muhsan) shall be flogged one hundred lashes and shall not be exiled. And the one who has (taken a slave girl in possession) and has not consummated (the marriage) with her shall be flogged one hundred lashes and shall be exiled.

key_terms.أُمْلِكَ: Literally 'was given ownership' — refers to the act of entering a valid marriage contract (or acquiring a slave girl), without necessarily completing it through consummation.
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ: The hadd punishment of one hundred lashes for fornication (zina) for the unmarried (ghair muhsan).
key_terms.يُحْصَنْ: To be muhsan — in the state of marital protection/fortification through a valid, consummated marriage. This status triggers the more severe hadd punishment.
key_terms.يُنْفَى: Banishment/exile — an additional punishment applied to the one who has a marriage contract but has not consummated it.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on the punishment for fornication for married and unmarried persons according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) articulates a legal ruling distinguishing the punishment for fornication based on marital status. An unmarried offender receives one hundred lashes without exile, while one who has contracted marriage (or acquired a slave girl) without consummation receives one hundred lashes plus banishment. This ruling reflects a graduated approach in Islamic penal law where full marital status (ihsan), which requires consummation, is a prerequisite for the capital hadd punishment of stoning, and this hadith addresses the intermediate categories.
